1.title: Finding My Voice

1.content: After years of suffering in silence, I finally found the courage to speak out. This app helped me connect with support services that changed my life.

laws.infoBanner: These laws protect your rights. Tap any law to learn more.
laws.helpText: Contact FIDA Tanzania or local legal aid organizations for assistance with your case.

1.title: Law of Marriage Act, 1971
1.description: Provides for registration of marriages and annulment
1.content: This act establishes the legal framework for marriage in Tanzania, including rights of spouses and procedures for divorce.

2.title: HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2008
2.description: Protects rights of people living with HIV/AIDS
2.content: Includes provisions to prevent discrimination and sexual violence, particularly against women and vulnerable persons.

3.title: Penal Code
3.description: Criminal legislation including provisions on sexual offences
3.content: Sections 130-145 address sexual violence, although reforms are ongoing to strengthen protections.

4.title: Sexual Offences Special Provisions Act, 1998
4.content: Establishes special provisions for prosecution of sexual offences and protects victims.

5.title: Law of Personal Status, 1961
5.description: Islamic law governing personal status matters
5.content: Governs marriage, divorce, inheritance under Islamic law in Zanzibar.

6.title: Penal Code
6.description: Criminal legislation with provisions on sexual crimes
6.content: Contains sections addressing sexual violence and assault with specific cultural considerations.

information.headerSubtitle: Learn about your rights and protections
information.infoBanner: This information is provided for educational purposes to help you understand your rights and available protections.

policies.infoBanner: These international policies provide a framework for protecting women's rights globally.
policies.resourceText: Visit UN Women for more information

1.title: Istanbul Convention
1.content: The Convention on preventing and combating violence against women and domestic violence is a landmark treaty against human rights violations.

2.title: UN Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW)
2.content: An international bill of rights for women that emphasizes their freedom from sexual violence and exploitation.

3.title: Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action
3.content: A comprehensive framework for advancing gender equality and addressing violence against women globally.

rights.declarationText: All humans are born free and equal in dignity and rights. These rights are inalienable and protected by international law.
rights.tip1: Your rights cannot be taken away because of your gender
rights.tip2: You have the right to safety and protection from harm
rights.tip3: You deserve respect, dignity, and equal opportunity
rights.tip4: Seek help - there are resources and support available
rights.supportText: If your rights are being violated, reach out to support organizations and authorities who can help.

1.title: Right to Life
1.description: Everyone has the inherent right to life protected by law
1.content: This fundamental right includes protection from all forms of violence and threats to personal safety.

2.title: Right to Freedom from Torture and Cruel Treatment
2.description: No one shall be subjected to torture or cruel, inhuman treatment
2.content: Sexual violence, domestic violence, and physical abuse constitute violations of this right.

3.title: Right to Equality and Non-Discrimination
3.description: All people are equal before the law regardless of sex
3.content: Gender-based discrimination that leads to violence is a violation of this fundamental right.

4.title: Right to Physical Integrity
4.description: Every person has the right to preserve their bodily integrity
4.content: Protection from sexual violence and assault is essential to protecting bodily autonomy.
